correctness.rationale: For n>=3 all edge-coordinate projections onto ker(B) have squared norm (n-2)/n because BB^T=nI-J. The telescoping prefix conservation identities force the bound t <= min_k beta_k/[k(n-k)]; an explicit constant t plus nonnegative adjacent-edge residual flow attains it. All and only the minimizing cuts force zero residual crossing edges. Each complementary block admits a strictly positive interior flow, so the exact incenter locus is a product of full-dimensional block flow polytopes with dimensions (d-1)(d-2)/2. Unit-source/sink parity and asymptotics follow. The separate exact-rational, numerical SVD, rank, and LP checker passed 63 general cases; analytical proof is independently reconstructed in RESULT.md.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new theorem uses a cut-conservation lower bound plus the constant projected coordinate-normal norm and then proves a product decomposition of the entire optimal-center face. Each step is needed: the listed prior volume/face/deformation theorems do not imply the metric statement by restriction or relabeling.

evidence: The flow/Tesler identification in Mészáros–Morales–Rhoades (arxiv:1409.8566, Section 1.2) is by coordinate permutation, but its theorems cover face structure and volume.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Tesler matrix coordinates are orthogonally permuted flow coordinates, so a matching Tesler inball theorem would be equivalent; the inspected face/deformation theorems do not supply one. Searches for insphere, Chebyshev center and inradius under these aliases did not identify a covering result; this is not proof of uniqueness.

evidence: Dugan (arxiv:2409.15519, Sections 4–5) enumerates face vectors and vertices, not Euclidean ball radii.
Corteel–Kim–Mészáros (arxiv:1612.00102, Theorems 1.1–1.3) give normalized volume products, not incenter tables.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact previously tabulated all-dimension radius or center-dimension values were identified. Generic LP computation of a finite case or f-vector table cannot by itself cover the closed formula for all positive-prefix real netflows. Search incompleteness remains a priority risk.

originality.rationale: Inspected same-object primary papers provide normalized volume (arxiv:1612.00102), flow/Tesler face structure (arxiv:1409.8566), deformation cones (arxiv:2212.11423), and CRY f-vector formulas (arxiv:2409.15519), but none gives the claimed edge-metric Euclidean inradius and complete factorization/dimension of all optimal ball centers. Established lower-bounded-flow feasibility and graph-effective-resistance ingredients are not claimed as inventions. A possible equivalent formulation in older max-min network-flow or Chebyshev-center literature is an explicitly retained priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical max-min fair flow theory may encode the exact optimal common edge floor as a standard specialization.
A complete literature survey of older Chebyshev-center and intrinsic flow-polytope metrics has not been carried out.
Different embeddings of integrally equivalent polytopes need not preserve inradii; the claim intentionally fixes edge-flow coordinates.

value.rationale: The result resolves a natural exact Euclidean invariant for a classical flow-polytope family and supplies a complete phase-stratified locus of all inball centers, including an explicit product decomposition at bottleneck cuts. In the unit-source/unit-sink case, the inradius has sharp 4/n^2 decay and centers occupy asymptotically half of the intrinsic polytope dimension, with a nonuniqueness threshold n=6. This geometric information is not a routine restatement of the established Catalan volume or face-count formulas; it also works for arbitrary strictly positive-prefix real netflows.
